adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Switching live span keys from SET to ZSET makes rolling deploys and rollbacks fail with WRONGTYPE until every in-flight key expires

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes span buffer Redis data structures from SET to ZSET for the same key pattern `span-buf:s:{...}:...`: `buffer.py` switches `p.sadd(...)` to `p.zadd(...)` (around line ~197) and `_load_segment_data` switches `sscan` to `zscan`; the Lua script likewise switches `scard/sunionstore` to `zcard/zunionstore` and uses `zpopmin`. Existing in-flight keys created by the old code as SETs would still exist during a rolling deploy/rollback, and the new code would issue ZSET commands against them, which in Redis yields `WRONGTYPE` until those keys expire. No compatibility handling (e.g., renaming keys, dual-read, type check/convert) is shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Insertion and eviction run in separate non-transactional pipelines, so a crash or concurrent flush can leave or emit an uncapped segment after the load-time count guard was removed

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `process_spans` in `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py` now uses a single non-transactional pipeline to `zadd` span payloads with a score (end_timestamp_precise). There is no eviction/capping logic shown in `buffer.py` at/around that insertion site, so the claim that “insertion and eviction run in separate non-transactional pipelines” in `buffer.py` is not supported by the diff. The removed load-time span-count guard in `_load_segment_data` is verifiable, but the stated crash/concurrent-flush scenario involving a separate eviction pipeline cannot be confirmed from the changes shown (capping/eviction appears only in the Lua script).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 — ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM, so replayed payloads present in both sets acquire inflated timestamps and can evict genuinely newer spans

adjudication.rationale: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua the code switched from set unions (SUNIONSTORE) to sorted-set unions using `zunionstore(set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)` / `zunionstore(set_key, 2, set_key, parent_key)` without specifying an `AGGREGATE` option. In Redis, ZUNIONSTORE defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`, so if the same payload member exists in both inputs its score (used here as `end_timestamp_precise`) will be summed, producing an incorrect inflated timestamp. Since later logic enforces a size cap via `zpopmin` based on these scores, incorrect scores can distort which spans are considered oldest/newest for eviction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Lowering redirect traversal to 1000 silently splits deeper or adversarial traces at an intermediate parent instead of the actual segment root

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the redirect-walk loop bound is reduced from `for i = 0, 10000 do` to `for i = 0, 1000 do`. The loop updates `set_span_id` by following `hget` redirects until it reaches a fixed point, then uses that `set_span_id` to union span sets (`zunionstore`) and write the redirect (`hset main_redirect_key, span_id, set_span_id`). If the redirect chain is deeper than 1000, the loop will terminate due to the new bound rather than reaching the true root, and the script will proceed with an intermediate `set_span_id`, effectively splitting/incorrectly joining very deep traces without any error or fallback handling. This matches the finding and is a correctness change introduced by the diff.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — A caller-supplied negative cursor reaches Django negative QuerySet slicing, which is unsupported and turns the advertised advanced path into a repeatable 500
matched_golden_ids: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments describe the same underlying bug: a negative offset/cursor value is allowed to reach Django QuerySet slicing (particularly on the prev-cursor path), resulting in unsupported negative slicing and potential 500 errors due to lack of clamping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py:126 — The tests only retrofit timestamps and never exceed the 1000-span boundary, leaving eviction selection and enforcement completely unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new eviction/enforcement behavior in `add-buffer.lua`: it tracks `span_count` for a sorted set and trims to 1000 members via `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)` when `span_count > 1000`. The updated tests in `tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py` (and others) only add the new required `end_timestamp_precise` field to existing small span batches; nothing in the diff shows a test that creates >1000 spans or verifies that eviction occurs and that it evicts the expected members (lowest score/oldest by `end_timestamp_precise`). That’s a concrete gap in coverage for the new logic, not a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Reusing existing span-buffer keys as sorted sets without a versioned migration makes pre-deploy SET data trigger Redis WRONGTYPE failures during rollout.

adjudication.rationale: The diff switches the Redis data type for existing span-buffer keys from SETs to ZSETs without changing the key name/version. In `buffer.py`, `process_spans` now writes `span-buf:s:{...}:{...}` with `zadd` (was `sadd`), and `_load_segment_data` reads with `zscan` (was `sscan`). The Lua script `add-buffer.lua` likewise changes `scard/sunionstore` to `zcard/zunionstore` on the same `span-buf:s:{...}:...` keys. During a rolling deploy, preexisting keys created by old code as SETs will be accessed by new code as ZSETs (or vice versa), which in Redis triggers `WRONGTYPE` errors. No key versioning or migration logic is shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — Hard-coding the eviction limit to 1000 ignores the public SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans setting, so callers can no longer configure this boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a hard cap in `add-buffer.lua` that trims the Redis sorted set to 1000 entries (`if span_count > 1000 then ... zpopmin ...`). In `spans/buffer.py`, span payloads are now stored in Redis via `zadd(...)` and the prior Python-side enforcement of `self.max_segment_spans` in `_load_segment_data` was removed. There is no wiring in the diff that ties the Lua cap (1000) to `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans`, so any configurability via that setting would no longer control the actual stored span count. This is a concrete, diff-grounded mismatch/regression in configurability/behavior, though it’s not provably a correctness defect without seeing how `max_segment_spans` is intended to be used externally.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:79 — Selecting OptimizedCursorPaginator for a datetime ordering makes any nonempty optimized audit-log request raise TypeError when the paginator calls math.floor on a datetime.

adjudication.rationale: `organization_auditlogs.py` now conditionally uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key`, it does `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` and then casts to `int`. If `self.key` resolves to the `datetime` attribute of the audit log model (as implied by `order_by="-datetime"`), `value` will be a `datetime`, and calling `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on a `datetime` will raise `TypeError`. This would break any optimized-paginated request that reaches cursor construction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — The advertised negative-offset cursor path passes a negative slice to Django QuerySet, which rejects negative indexing and returns a server error instead of a page.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code intentionally sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and slices the queryset with `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices (negative start/stop), and will raise an error rather than returning results. The diff also adds comments claiming negative slicing is safe/handled by Django, but the actual code path would trigger a server error if exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — Reading optimized_pagination outside AuditLogQueryParamSerializer leaves the new public query parameter untyped and silently treats invalid values as false.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the new behavior is gated by `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` rather than being parsed/validated alongside the other query params (which are built into `query` earlier in the method). This means any value other than the exact string "true" (including invalid/typo values) will be silently treated as disabled, and the parameter is effectively unvalidated/undocumented by the existing query-param parsing path. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded review concern, but it’s not a clear correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — The advanced negative-offset path passes a negative slice boundary to a Django QuerySet, causing an unhandled assertion error instead of returning a page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:184 — A negative previous-page offset remains negative in BasePaginator and is passed to a Django QuerySet slice, causing an unhandled assertion error.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` the new logic sets `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, so when `cursor.is_prev` is true a negative `cursor.offset` is preserved and used in `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and raises an `AssertionError` for negative slicing, so this change can cause an unhandled exception if a prev-page cursor with a negative offset is provided (and the diff elsewhere explicitly indicates intent to allow negative offsets via comments in `Cursor`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — The generic paginator hard-codes numeric key conversion even though its only caller supplies a datetime ordering key, leaking cursor value type assumptions across the endpoint boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` which unconditionally applies `math.floor/ceil` and casts to `int` on `getattr(item, self.key)`, assuming the key is numeric. In `organization_auditlogs.py`, this new paginator is conditionally used with `order_by="-datetime"`, implying the cursor key will be a datetime field. Applying `math.floor/ceil` to a datetime value would raise a type error, so the new paginator leaks a numeric cursor-value assumption into an endpoint that paginates by datetime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845 — OptimizedCursorPaginator copies BasePaginator.get_result wholesale instead of isolating its slice policy, creating parallel pagination implementations that must stay synchronized.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class that re-implements a full `get_result(...)` method (cursor setup, hits counting, queryset building, slicing, prev handling, reversing, and `build_cursor(...)` call) rather than delegating to/overriding only the slicing behavior. This creates a second pagination implementation path alongside the existing paginator logic (e.g., the slicing logic modified earlier in `paginator.py`), increasing the risk the two will diverge and require manual synchronization. This is a maintainability/architecture concern evidenced directly by the large duplicated `get_result` body in the new class.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — The optimized_pagination option bypasses AuditLogQueryParamSerializer, splitting query validation and schema ownership between raw request parsing and the serializer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new query parameter `optimized_pagination` that is read directly from `request.GET` (`use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`) and used to change pagination behavior, rather than being part of the existing query/serializer-driven validation flow. While this doesn’t bypass validation for the existing audited filters (those still go through the prior `query` object), it does split query-param schema/ownership by adding an unvalidated, behavior-changing flag outside the serializer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — ZPOPMIN materializes every evicted payload in the Lua VM even though its result is discarded, causing avoidable Redis memory and CPU spikes on oversized merges

adjudication.rationale: In `add-buffer.lua` the new oversize-trimming logic does `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` without capturing the return value. `ZPOPMIN` returns the removed members+scores, so even if the Lua code discards it, Redis still has to construct that reply for the Lua call. On large evictions (when `span_count` is far above 1000) this can add avoidable CPU/memory overhead during merges. This is a performance concern introduced by the diff rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:449 — Removing the span-count cutoff lets oversized or legacy zsets materialize and JSON-decode thousands of tiny spans despite the configured max_segment_spans guard

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Python-side span-count guard in `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data`: the prior check `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans: ... del payloads[key] ...` is deleted and replaced with an unconditional `payloads[key].extend(span for span, _ in zscan_values)`, while only the byte-size cutoff remains. Although `add-buffer.lua` now trims joined zsets to 1000 entries, `process_spans` in `buffer.py` writes directly via `zadd(...)` with no trimming, and legacy/oversized zsets may already exist. This makes it possible for `_load_segment_data` to materialize and later decode far more spans than `max_segment_spans` intended, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Switching live buffer keys from Redis sets to sorted sets without migration makes rolling deploys hit WRONGTYPE and repeatedly fail Kafka processing until legacy keys expire

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Redis data structure for the same live keys without any compatibility handling. In `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py`, `process_spans` now writes to `set_key = f"span-buf:s:{{{project_and_trace}}}:{parent_span_id}"` using `ZADD` (`p.zadd(...)`) instead of `SADD`, and `_load_segment_data` switches from `SSCAN` to `ZSCAN`. In the Lua script `add-buffer.lua`, operations on the same `span-buf:s:{...}:...` keys switch from `SCARD/SUNIONSTORE` to `ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE`. Since the key names are unchanged, a rolling deploy where some instances still create/use Redis Sets and others expect Sorted Sets will cause Redis `WRONGTYPE` errors when a new instance runs `Z*` commands on an existing Set key (or vice versa) until those keys expire. This can plausibly break span buffering/consumption during deployment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 — ZUNIONSTORE's default SUM makes Kafka replays inflate timestamp scores so eviction can retain replayed old spans and discard newer spans

adjudication.rationale: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua the change from set unions to sorted-set unions uses `zunionstore` without specifying an `AGGREGATE` option (e.g., MAX/MIN). Redis defaults `ZUNIONSTORE` aggregation to `SUM`, so if the same span payload (member) exists in both `set_key` and `span_key`/`parent_key` (e.g., due to reprocessing/replay recreating a temporary set that later gets merged again), the resulting score becomes the sum of timestamps rather than the intended timestamp. Since the script later evicts with `zpopmin` based on score, inflated scores can cause older spans to look newer and affect eviction correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Redirect traversal silently stops after 1001 hops without detecting exhaustion so deep traces can be split instead of surfacing a recoverable error

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` the redirect traversal loop limit was reduced from `for i = 0, 10000 do` to `for i = 0, 1000 do` (inclusive = 1001 iterations). There is still no check after the loop to detect that the redirect chain did not terminate (i.e., `new_set_span` never became nil or stable), so traversal can silently stop at the cap and proceed using a potentially incorrect `set_span_id`. This can lead to incomplete joining of deep redirect chains (splitting/fragmenting traces) with no surfaced error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — The optimized audit-log path has no behavioral test, so numeric cursor conversion of its datetime sort key fails on any populated page without detection.

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then `math.floor/ceil(value)` cast to `int`. In the audit log endpoint, the optimized path paginates with `order_by='-datetime'`, so the key is a datetime field; `math.floor/ceil` on a `datetime` object will raise a `TypeError` on any non-empty result page. This is a concrete runtime correctness break introduced by the diff (tests absence just makes it undetected).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 — No negative-offset test exercises the advertised advanced path, which passes an invalid negative slice to a Django QuerySet instead of paginating.

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` explicitly allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, and then does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (negative slice) (added block near the end of `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`). Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing and will raise an error, so this “advanced path” is broken if a client supplies a negative cursor offset. The diff also shows no tests added to exercise this negative-offset branch, making the issue unguarded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — The tests only add identical timestamps to tiny fixtures and never cross the 1,000-span boundary, leaving oldest-first eviction and the exact cap unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new sorted-set behavior and a hard cap/eviction path in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` (`zcard`/`zunionstore` and `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", ...) end`). The updated tests only introduce `end_timestamp_precise` with the same constant value (e.g., `1700000000.0`) and the fixtures shown are small (a handful of spans), so they do not exercise the >1000 boundary or validate that `zpopmin` evicts the oldest-by-score entries and enforces the exact 1000 cap. This is a specific missing-coverage issue for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — No test configures max_segment_spans after enforcement moved to a hard-coded Lua limit, so the existing constructor option can be silently ignored.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes enforcement of `self.max_segment_spans` in `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data` (the block that checked `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` is deleted) and replaces span storage with a Redis sorted set plus a hard-coded cap in Lua: `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000) end`. This makes any configurable `max_segment_spans` value (previously used for enforcement) effectively ignored in favor of a fixed limit of 1000, which is a behavior change and can silently violate configuration expectations. The tests in the diff also do not exercise/configure a non-default `max_segment_spans` to catch this mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — No boundary test covers the lowered redirect traversal limit at depths 1,000 and 1,001, leaving deep segment joining behavior unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly lowers the redirect traversal loop limit in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` from `for i = 0, 10000 do` to `for i = 0, 1000 do`, which changes behavior for redirect chains deeper than 1000. The added/modified tests in the diff are Python tests around span buffering and Redis zset usage, but none exercise or assert behavior around redirect-chain depth near this new boundary (e.g., depth 1000 vs 1001). This is a specific, diff-grounded gap in coverage for a nontrivial behavioral change, but it is not itself a directly verifiable defect from the diff alone.
